domains.name: Planning, Budgeting and Forecasting
domains.description: CFO agenda · planning-maturity curve · driver-based, rolling, ZBB · simulation · analytics ladder
domains.scope: The CFO's forward-looking engine: planning philosophy and maturity, budget methodologies, driver-based and constraint-based planning, scenario & simulation, rolling forecasts, and the CFO agenda that frames it all.

items.title: CFO agenda pillars
items.text: (verbatim): "See the future first" · "Bring one version of the truth" · "Instill stakeholder confidence" · "Make it easier to do business with us" · "Improve finance effectiveness" · "Protect value" · "Strategy to execution discipline". The CFO's shift: from managing cost to optimizing performance; from "are these numbers right?" to "how do we use these numbers to better our business?".

items.title: Value-lever cascade
items.text: — shareholder value → profitable revenue growth · cost reduction · balance-sheet improvement · free cash flow → operational levers (rolling forecast on granular timely data, adaptive planning, bottom-up revenue/cost forecasting, faster variance analysis, shared-services expansion, faster close with world-class risk & compliance).

items.title: PB&F performance loop
items.text: — goal-setting → planning/budgeting → forecast → reporting → analysis → optimization → value creation; underpinned by leadership, governance/risk/change, people-process-technology-data, and a single-version-of-truth information platform.

items.title: Persona analysis
items.text: — finance stakeholders (CFO, corporate controller, audit/tax/treasury heads, head of FP&A, head of management reporting, head of shared services) profiled by objectives, information needs/KPIs and pain points; feeds value boards and value maps.

items.title: 4-level planning-maturity curve
items.text: — 1 Ad-hoc (Excel, no variance reporting) → 2 Traditional (manual annual budgeting, static, "extensive sandbagging", silo budgets) → 3 Coherent & Diagnostic (driver-based planning, rolling forecast, workflow-controlled, multidimensional variance, financial-operational linkage, feedback loop) → 4 Prescriptive (predictive, advanced scenarios, risk/opportunity identification, suggested decision options). Target: one maturity leap per year.

items.title: Budget methodologies
items.text: — top-down target-driven (flagged insensitive to business) · bottom-up with consolidation · driver-based · rolling forecast · adaptive/lean with quarterly reviews · zero-based ("history-independent demand-aligned budget"; savings evidence: SG&A −10–25%, often within six months) · activity-based; philosophy shift "budgeting & planning" → "planning & budgeting" (leaner annual budget, quarterly review).

items.title: Driver-based planning areas
items.text: — revenue, COGS, production, material & resource requirements, factory overhead, selling/distribution/admin, capex, workforce, and full P&L / balance-sheet / cash-flow planning.

items.title: Constraint-based planning
items.text: — unconstrained sales plan → capacity-check chain (own production, vendor, storage, transportation, labour, warehouse-provider) → constrained plan; material planning across 3 BOM levels with automatic feedback; constraint-derived capex plan; capacity-utilization decision bands (50–70% realign / 70–90% partial outsourcing / @90% invest).

items.title: Planning calendar pattern
items.text: — Q1 AOP actualization · Q2 full-year forecast + FCF/CCC risks & opportunities · Q3 balance-sheet bottom-up · Q4 AOP-level full-year forecast; strategic plan (annual) + AOP + quarterly updates.

Concepts & processes.heading: Scenario analysis, simulation & the analytics ladder

items.title: Analytics capability ladder
items.text: — Retrospective (baseline history: metric bank, reports) → Correctional (sense & respond: exceptions, diagnostics) → Anticipatory (predict: scenario, predictive & stochastic models) → Cognitive (optimize & prescribe: ML/AI, optimization).

items.title: Deterministic vs stochastic simulation
items.text: — deterministic: linear rule-driven, ~1yr data, ~1 month time-to-value · stochastic: multivariate over a full business cycle (3–5yrs), randomness & causality, confidence-level prediction, exogenous drivers (FX, commodity, fuel, customer credit rating), 2–3 months time-to-value.

items.title: Simulation use cases
items.text: — P&L simulation (discount/promo spend, volume, FX/commodity/labour de-risking); working-capital-lever simulation (DSO→sales/profit/cash/bad-debt; DIO→carrying cost; DPO→cash flow); credit-terms simulation (cash-discount % + credit-period days → opportunity cost, net value unlock); financial-policy simulation (parametric policy change before finalizing).

items.title: Finance-transformation delivery lifecycle
items.text: — business case (KPI benchmarking, value-unlock, ROI) → process diagnostic & maturity assessment → redesign (AS-IS → gap vs leading practice → TO-BE) → tool assessment → implementation (blueprint → realization → go-live) → adoption & benefits realization; governance = steering committee / change control / PM / core teams.

domains.name: Cost and Profitability Management
domains.description: Standard costing & variances · ABC/TD-ABC · cost-to-serve · true margin · shared-services chargeback
domains.scope: The costing machinery: standard costing and the full variance taxonomy, marginal vs absorption, activity-based and time-driven costing, cost-to-serve, shared-services chargeback, capacity management — feeding customer/product profitability down to true margin.

items.title: Standard cost
items.text: (professional-body definition, verbatim): "the planned unit cost of the product, component or service produced in a period… main use is in performance measurement, control, stock valuation and in the establishment of selling prices"; >70% of UK manufacturers use standard costing.

items.title: 4-element system
items.text: — set standards (historical records or engineering/time-and-motion studies) → compare actual vs standard → analyse & report variances → investigate & act; philosophy: management by exception.

items.title: Variance taxonomy
items.text: — material: price + usage (usage subdivides into mix and yield — process industries); labour: rate + efficiency; variable overhead: expenditure + efficiency; fixed overhead: expenditure + volume (explains under/over-recovery); sales variances in contribution terms; planning vs operational split (external-factor vs management-controllable). Known drawbacks: conflicts with JIT/zero-waste, stale standards, complex overhead variances.

items.title: Marginal vs absorption costing
items.text: — marginal: variable cost only, contribution = revenue − variable cost of sales, fixed costs as period costs; absorption: fixed production overhead absorbed into unit cost (inventory-standard compliant); profit difference = fixed overhead in opening vs closing inventory.

items.title: Two-stage ABC
items.text: — stage 1: cost drivers trace input costs into cost pools; stage 2: pools into products; worked driver set: production runs → set-up cost; receipts → receiving; deliveries → packing; production orders → engineering; machine hours → machine overheads; effect: overhead shifts materially to low-volume complex products.

items.title: Time-driven ABC
items.text: — resource pools → capacity cost rates → time equations per activity; "duration drivers usually far more accurate than transaction drivers"; applied to warehousing & transportation costing.

items.title: Cost build-up ladder
items.text: — Prime Cost → Works Cost → Cost of Goods Manufactured → COGS → Cost of Sale; analysis dimensions product / customer / channel / geography; wrapped in change management & governance.

items.title: Cost-to-serve model (CPG)
items.text: — supply-chain model per customer demand type (Warehoused / Cross-Dock / Direct-Store-Delivery); warehouse activities with UoM drivers (unloading & putaway #cases, storage case-days, pick&pack labour-hours, ship-to-customer case-km); CTS customer characteristics: order variability, average order size, credit period; span across plan-source-make-deliver-service incl. opportunity cost of capital blocked in AR & inventory.

items.title: Profitability waterfall to true margin
items.text: — gross external revenue → −discounts/returns/trade promotion → net external revenue → −prime → works → COGM → COGS → COS → net margin → true margin after financial elements (inventory blockage, AR blockage, opportunity costs).

items.title: Cost classification matrix
items.text: — each cost component classified by incidence (pre/post-factory), ladder position, nature (fixed/variable/semi), customer influence (full/partial/indifferent) and allocation complexity (high/medium/low).

items.title: Capacity measurement
items.text: — resource supply at practical capacity vs budgeted/actual demand per product; gaps flag capacity-constrained resources (invest / outsource / reschedule) or excess capacity (restructure); driver restructuring exposes idle-capacity cost (worked example: $1,000 incurred vs $860 allocated).

items.title: Shared-services chargeback
items.text: — service catalogue (GL → activity → service code); methodology 1: allocate actual expenses (no recovery variance, consumers "feel helpless") vs methodology 2: standard/negotiated activity price (provider as profit center, recovery variance, drives demand management — demand-side levers deliver >40% of the cost opportunity); allocation models waterfall / recursive / reciprocal; leading practice posts ABC results to the GL at month-end.

domains.name: Working Capital and Treasury
domains.description: CCC via P2P/F2F/O2C · treasury roles · reverse factoring · debtor analytics · bad-debt value mgmt
domains.scope: Cash and the cycle that creates it: treasury's strategic role, working-capital governance and programs, the CCC managed through P2P / forecast-to-fulfill / order-to-cash, financing instruments, debtor analytics and bad-debt value management.

items.title: Treasury's strategic shift
items.text: — from back-office guardian to strategic value creator (84% report expanded role over 5 years; 37% of treasurers sit in the C-suite; 46% act as internal consultants); lead-role league table (% of orgs): bank relationship management 94 · short-term borrowing 86 · long-term funding 85 · short-term investing 77 · financial risk 53 · working-capital management 49 · FP&A 38 · ERM 32.

items.title: Working-capital governance
items.text: — primary responsibility: shared finance + functions 40% / CFO 33% / treasury 20%; treasury leads payables (50%) and receivables (45%); inventory sits with operations (5%); 59% run a WC programme; 64% use WC improvement as internal funding; only 42% apply a WACC hurdle to working capital.

items.title: CCC process triad
items.text: — cash conversion cycle controlled through three integrated processes: Purchase-to-Pay (requisition → source → contract → receive → invoice → pay), Forecast-to-Fulfill (S&OP: forecast, plan supply/inventory/production, store, produce, ship), Order-to-Cash (contract, credit check, order, ship, invoice, collect); improvement staging Recovery → Optimization → Transformation; classic barriers: fear of damaging customer/supplier relationships, discounts given without early payment, metrics that ignore cash, unclear cross-functional ownership.

items.title: Financing instruments
items.text: — reverse factoring / supply-chain finance (bank pays supplier early against buyer's stronger credit); factoring (recourse/non-recourse, disclosed/undisclosed; admin + finance ~80% advance + risk control); bill discounting (individual bills, with recourse, on-balance-sheet) vs factoring (whole-turnover, off-balance-sheet when full); forfaiting (export receivables, aval guarantee, without recourse); e-invoicing (accelerates DSO — payment-timing pitfall: invoice date vs receipt date); cash pooling, treasury centralization, single-channel payment routing, credit insurance, money-market floats.

items.title: Bad-debt value management
items.text: — lifecycle: access screening (NPV-based acceptance; ~30% of applicants reassigned under value-based screening) → in-life collection (willingness × ability-to-pay segments with tailored treatments) → recovery (multi-agency allocation by recovery likelihood, reconnection incentives, debt sale last); shift from bad-debt minimization to value management; hardest barrier: finance/sales/marketing incentive conflicts.

items.title: Credit policy formulation
items.text: — internal drivers (sales growth, WC investment stance, cost of capital) × external (customer credit appetite, competitor norms, bargaining power); behavioural payer segmentation; deterministic provisioning models. (Carried from v1.0 debtor analytics; the landing adds the instrument & program layer.)

domains.name: Consolidation, Close and Statutory
domains.description: Eliminations · currency layers · close-control extensions · IAS 36 · GST · disclosure
domains.scope: Group truth: the consolidation and close process chain, close-control extensions, statutory disclosure, and the accounting-standard events (impairment, indirect-tax regimes) that hit the statements.

items.title: Close-process chain
items.text: (suite-definition verbatim) — local/BU sub-consolidation → intercompany transaction management (elimination + matching) → currency translation & revaluation → group consolidation on shared dimensions (legal entity, account) → audited enterprise view → statutory statements (GAAP/IFRS, XBRL) + management packs with commentary → variance analysis vs targets.

items.title: Close-control extensions
items.text: — reconciliation management, intercompany activity management, journal-entry control, financial-control testing, tax-data provisioning.

items.title: Consolidation solution requirements (v1.0)
items.text: — automated intragroup eliminations, journal adjustments with audit trail, multi-currency at scenario-specific rates, multi-layer adjustments (country, hub, other), account-mapping chains ERP → consolidation → group, reporting packs (P&L, B/S, CF + intercompany, asset movements, EBITA reconciliation).

items.title: IAS 36 impairment process
items.text: — indicator assessment each reporting date (external: rates, market changes, market cap < net assets; internal: restructuring, obsolescence); goodwill & indefinite-life intangibles tested annually; recoverable amount = higher of fair value less costs to sell and value in use (pre-tax cash flows from approved budgets, exclude uncommitted restructurings, terminal value with steady/declining growth); CGU logic (smallest independent cash-inflow group; goodwill allocated no larger than an operating segment); loss allocation goodwill-first then pro-rata; reversals capped, goodwill reversal prohibited; disclosure of assumptions, headroom, sensitivity.

items.title: Dual-GST mechanics

domains.name: Statement Analysis and Valuation
domains.description: Ratio taxonomy · restatement plays · DCF ↔ economic profit · target multiples · M&A pricing
domains.scope: Reading and pricing the enterprise: the canonical ratio taxonomy, analytical restatement before comparison, enterprise DCF and its economic-profit twin, residual income, target multiples, M&A pricing, and ratio-based risk models.

items.title: Ratio-analysis discipline
items.text: — four canonical categories: activity, liquidity, solvency (leverage), profitability ; three comparison modes (cross-sectional vs peers, time-series, combined); two directions: bottom-up (many ratios, look for changes) and top-down ROE/DuPont decomposition (start with ROE, explain via components).

items.title: Analytical restatement (first-class process)
items.text: — restate before comparing: LIFO↔FIFO via the LIFO reserve; capitalization vs expensing; off-balance-sheet financing & securitization add-backs; equity-method vs full-consolidation recasts (evidenced with a beverage major and its bottler — an FMCG anchor); purchase vs pooling conversion; FX effects on levels/trends; changing-price adjustments; revenue-recognition quality checks.

items.title: Enterprise DCF (4 steps)
items.text: — forecast FCF → estimate WACC → continuing value → analyze; three-forecast-period pattern: 5 years detailed + 10 years key-driver (six inputs: revenue growth, EBITA margin, cash tax rate, net PPE %, other IC %, goodwill) + perpetuity via the value-driver formula (ROIC on new investment, NOPLAT growth); consistency discipline g = r × b; model self-checks: balance sheet balances, NOPLAT & invested-capital reconciliations, economic-profit and FCF valuations must be equal .

items.title: Economic-profit family
items.text: — equivalence theorem BVIC + ΣPV(EP) = ΣPV(FCF); EVA as dollar surplus closest to NPV; "growth per se does not create value — only reinvestment above the cost of capital does"; MVA = market value − capital invested; documented failure modes: negative EVA in heavy-investment growth phases, year-to-year EVA gaming, risk-induced value loss.

items.title: Residual income / multistage equity models
items.text: — dividend-discount base and horizon forms; multistage growth (three-phase, simplified two-rate); residual-income model P0 = B0 + Σ(ROE−r)·B/(1+r)^t with ROE fading to steady state via an autoregressive process.

items.title: Relative valuation
items.text: — multiples vary for four reasons (value-driver differences, accounting differences, cyclicality, mispricing); value drivers distill to return on capital, cost of capital, growth, duration of growth; target ("fair") multiples derived from DCF-equivalent formulas; comparability toolkit (maintenance capex for depreciation, goodwill handling, pension strip-outs, lease capitalization, exceptionals).

items.title: M&A pricing
items.text: — method triad: asset-oriented, income-oriented (DCF; terminal value often >50% of NPV), multiples; synergy framework: total synergy = V(C) − V(A) − V(B); acquisition premium (often 40–60%) = seller's synergy premium; deal success requires NPV-positive buyer's premium.

items.title: Ratio-based risk models
items.text: — bankruptcy prediction (Z-score lineage; most significant predictors: cash flow/total debt, total debt/total assets, NWC/total assets), bond-rating models (coverage, leverage, size, subordination), beta-prediction models — all built on the same four ratio categories plus earnings variability and size.

Metrics & KPIs.heading: Core ratios (verbatim)
tables: Current assets ÷ current liabilities (≈2 rule of thumb); (cash + securities + receivables) ÷ current liabilities (≈1)
Average age of inventory = inventory ÷ (COGS/365); average collection period = AR ÷ (sales/365); fixed & total asset turnover
Debt ratio = total liabilities ÷ total assets; D/E = LT debt ÷ common equity; times interest earned = EBIT ÷ interest (3–5); fixed-charge coverage
ROA = NI ÷ total assets; ROE = earnings to common ÷ common equity; EPS (weighted-average, diluted rules); P/E

Metrics & KPIs.heading: Valuation formulas (verbatim)
tables: (1 − t)·EBIT + Δdeferred taxes; from NI: NI + (1−t)·interest + deferred taxes − (1−t)·non-operating income
NOPLAT − ΔNOWC − ΔNFA; from CF statement: CFO + (1−t)·interest − CFI (simplified)
V_T = (1 − g/ROIC)·NOPLAT_T+1 ÷ (WACC − g); if ROIC = WACC then NOPLAT/WACC
EP = (ROIC − WACC) × invested capital; EVA worked case: ROC 12.77%, WACC 8.85%, capital 29,500 ⇒ EVA 1,154.5 (currency M)
(Adjusted EBIT(1−t) + non-cash charges) ÷ capital invested; (ROE − COE) × equity invested
COE = risk-free + β × equity premium; WACC = market-value-weighted blend (worked: 4.5% + 0.99×5.5% = 10%; WACC 8.85%)
EV/Sales = (ROIC−g)/(ROIC(WACC−g))·(1−T)·M; EV/EBITDA = same ×(1−D); EV/EBIT = same; EV/NOPLAT = (ROIC−g)/(ROIC(WACC−g)); P/E = (ROE−g)/(ROE(COE−g)); P/B = (ROE−g)/(COE−g); PEG
EV = market cap + net debt + pensions + minorities + debt-deemed provisions; OpFCF = EBITDA − maintenance capex − maintenance ΔNWC
Reserve life = reserves ÷ production; finding cost per unit; reserve replacement ratio — reusable pattern for asset-reserve industries

items.title: Risk analytics shift
items.text: — from perception-driven assessment and 25-sample periodic audits to anomaly-driven 100%-population screening with continuous-monitoring dashboards; "perception of continuous monitoring" itself deters fraud; 42% of all frauds are collusive, 100% of financial frauds are collusive.

items.title: Canonical CPM suite (analyst definition, verbatim components)
items.text: — 1. Budgeting, Planning & Forecasting (financial-modelling engine, integrated P&L/BS/CF, workflow, audit trail, driver-network what-if) · 2. Profitability Modeling & Optimization (ABC/ABM to granular cost objects; extends to pricing/channel optimization) · 3. Strategy Management (goals → initiatives → KPIs; scorecards & strategy maps) · 4. Financial Consolidation & Close · 5. Financial/Statutory/Management Reporting & Disclosure; deployment split: office-of-finance CPM vs strategic CPM; extends into operational planning wherever driver-based planning is critical.

items.title: EPM process cycle
items.text: — stakeholder environment → market model → business model → business plan → business operations → business results, integrated with scenario analysis at model level and variance analysis at plan level feeding back.

items.title: Implementation methodology
items.text: — blueprint (AS-IS → TO-BE per planning area, workflow, security, naming conventions) → realization (build + integration test + power-user training) → cutover → go-live + hypercare; patterns: global template, phased releases (pilot → rollout), parallel run against legacy for one cycle; failure statistics: insufficient planning 67%, poor requirements 59%, poor estimation 54%; top failure reason: ineffective governance; recovery 2×2 (business value × recovery cost): salvage / reprioritize / transform / discontinue.

items.title: Allocation-engine mechanics
items.text: — calculation path line items → (resource drivers + splits) → activities → (activity drivers) → cost objects; four assignment types; driver analysis = back-calculation from targets; version/period/responsibility-center reference cube kept small; model lifecycle build → import → calculate → validate → report (never in parallel).

items.title: Strategy-management chain
items.text: — context → perspective (financial / consumer / customer / internal process / learning & growth) → objective → KPI (target, actual, status) → initiative (owner, tasks, milestones); strategy-execution gap causes: employees don't understand strategy, incentives not linked, data-version distrust.

items.title: Financial-management maturity (public-audit model)
items.text: — five aspects (governance & leadership, planning, decision support, monitoring & forecasting, reporting) × five levels; level 5 = anticipates challenges with sophisticated cost-base understanding; best-fit not additive; top level not always cost-effective.
